CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that began one week ago during a gymnastics class. She reports falling into an awkward position during a move. She states that any movement of the left shoulder causes pain. She attempted self-treatment with Tylenol for 2-3 days without relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with shoulder movement. No other systems discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prior surgery on left arm.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (taken for 2-3 days, discontinued due to ineffectiveness)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in gymnastics class.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient demonstrates pain with shoulder movement in multiple directions. X-ray of left shoulder obtained.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fracture or broken bone identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Assessment: Left shoulder joint injury.

Plan:
1. Ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week
2. Ice or heat pad for pain relief as needed
3. Rest left arm during healing period
4. Avoid heavy lifting and carrying weights; use right arm for 3-4 weeks
5. Alternative options: Advil or Aleve
6. Follow-up appointment in 3 weeks
7. Possible repeat x-ray if pain persists after 3 weeks
8. Patient may call for earlier appointment if needed
